prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: full playable level-map concept for the existing 2D snake game Snabbit.
Primary request: suggest a beautiful native-looking composition for a puzzle titled Reverse the Rhythm. The silhouette is one tall chipped tuning-fork asteroid, with a broad lower RIGHT crescent hollow, a small inner stone seed and a slanting narrow hinge leading into one large airy upper LEFT harp-shaped hollow. Two short living stone arch crossings punctuate the rising path. This is a map made from the original separate little game sprites, not scenic illustration.
Input images: image1 is the real sprite style reference, especially rounded faceted white boulders, charcoal stones, cyan gems, yellow stars and the chunky grey lever with orange/green knob. Images2 and3 are references for original authored level composition and negative space only.
Composition: portrait full map, directly overhead, 16 columns of staggered hex-grid cells and about 65 rising rows. Bottom-center entry. The route rises into the lower-right crescent, crosses a little two-cell living arch at the thin right-hand shoulder, sweeps gradually left around a chipped central stone seed and into the large upper-left hollow, then rises through a second two-cell arch at the upper tip. The two same-channel mechanical levers are visually obvious: one in the lower crescent, one on a tempting little inner shoulder of the upper hollow. Place three yellow stars at meaningful rising milestones, 12 cyan gems in irregular short knots with quiet spaces, and a tiny diamond in a summit side pocket. A tiny finish opening fits the narrow top.
Style: faithful crisp polished 2D original game sprites, white and charcoal asteroid chunks on a very dark navy star-space background. Touchable toy-like chunky levers, each roughly one rock footprint. Airy, organic, asymmetric, charming. Walls have varied thickness, chipped ends, scallops and different-sized hollows.
Constraints: route can only move upward diagonally left or right. No returning downward. No rectangular rooms. Living gates look like ordinary original rocks, perhaps dimmer when hidden; no permanent color coding or letter labels on walls. No UI overlays, no route line, no labels, no title text.
Avoid: repeated identical chambers, regular left-right zigzag, full-width horizontal wall strips, rail corridors, uniform gem trails, painted terrain/floors, 3D/isometric view.
